music_rep_aero_grade_1: Grade 1: 100 BPM, a note a click
music_rep_aero_grade_3: Grade 3: 72 BPM, two notes a click
music_rep_aero_grade_5: Grade 5: 66 BPM, four notes a click
music_rep_aero_pair_all_open: all open to the octave key
music_rep_aero_pair_first_palm: open to the first palm key
music_rep_aero_vib_4_at_80: Four a beat at 80 (the going rate)
music_rep_jam_note_horse_with_no_name: The recording's second chord is D6/9 over F#. Plain D here.
music_rep_jam_note_let_it_be: The recording changes chord every two beats. One a bar here.
music_rep_jam_note_sweet_home_alabama: The recording plays C and G in one bar, with Cadd9. Plain chords here.
music_rep_jam_note_zombie: The recording has D over F#. Plain D here.
music_rep_padrep_afrobeats_feel: Kick on 1 with pushes on the & of 2 and 3. The rim answers on the a of 1 and the & of 2 (the 3-3-2). Clap on 2 and 4, shaker sixteenths. One common version: producers vary it.
music_rep_padrep_afrobeats_fingers: Right hand the shaker (hats) sixteenths. Left index kick, left middle rim. The clap and conga (high tom) where they fall.
music_rep_padrep_amen_feel: Four bars: the third delays the last snare, the fourth rearranges everything and crashes.
music_rep_padrep_amen_fingers: Right index on the ride. Left index the snare and ghosts, left middle the kick.
music_rep_padrep_apache_feel: The snare answers itself on the & of 3 and the a of 4 (tempo approximate).
music_rep_padrep_backbeat_feel: Kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4.
music_rep_padrep_backbeat_fingers: Left index on kick, right index on snare.
music_rep_padrep_basic_rock_feel: The beat under a thousand songs (Billie Jean sits on it at about 117 BPM).
music_rep_padrep_blues_shuffle_feel: Hats on the first and third of every triplet (the long-short of a shuffle), kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4.
music_rep_padrep_boom_bap_2bar_feel: Two bars. The second answers the first.
music_rep_padrep_boom_bap_a_feel: The kick's second hit lands on the & of 2: the first push.
music_rep_padrep_boom_bap_b_feel: The generic hip-hop kick: four hits after the backbeat on 2.
music_rep_padrep_bossa_nova_feel: The surdo on the kick (soft pushes before 1 and 3), and the bossa clave on the cross-stick over two bars.
music_rep_padrep_bossa_nova_fingers: Right hand the hats. Left index the kick, left middle the rim. The pedal hat with a spare finger on 2 and 4.
music_rep_padrep_cold_sweat_feel: Clyde Stubblefield's funk: the backbeat on 2, the second snare pushed to the a of 3, ghosts between. Provisional: a teaching version, check it against the recording.
music_rep_padrep_cold_sweat_fingers: Right hand the hats. Left index the snare and its ghosts, left middle the kick.
music_rep_padrep_cumbia_feel: The guacharaca on the hats (one on the beat, two on the & and a), the llamador on 2 and 4. Players put the kick on every beat, on 2 and 4, or a tumbao: this one keeps it on the beat.
music_rep_padrep_cumbia_fingers: Right index and middle the guacharaca. Left index kick, left middle rim.
music_rep_padrep_dancehall_feel: The 3+3+2 split between kick (1 and the a of 1, 3 and the a of 3) and snare (the & of 2 and 4).
music_rep_padrep_dembow_feel: Four on the floor with the snare on the a of 1, the & of 2, and again.
music_rep_padrep_dilla_feel: Swung hats over a straight kick, and the snare pushed about 20 ms early: two feels at once.
music_rep_padrep_disco_feel: Four on the floor, the snare on 2 and 4, sixteenth hats that open on every &.
music_rep_padrep_disco_fingers: Right index and middle the hats, the middle opening on the &; left index kick, left middle snare.
music_rep_padrep_dnb_feel: Kick on 1 and the & of 3, snare on 2 and 4, fast.
music_rep_padrep_eighth_hats_feel: The backbeat with eighth hats over it.
music_rep_padrep_fill_one_beat_feel: Three bars of rock, then four sixteenth snares on beat 4 and back to 1.
music_rep_padrep_fill_one_beat_fingers: Fill: alternate both index fingers on the snare.
music_rep_padrep_fill_two_beats_feel: Sixteenths down the kit: snare, high, mid and low tom, then the downbeat.
music_rep_padrep_fill_two_beats_fingers: Alternate hands, right leading, across the pads from left to right.
music_rep_padrep_fingers_hats_ghosts: Right hand the hats. Left index the snare and ghosts, left middle the kick.
music_rep_padrep_fingers_kick_clap: Left index on the kick, right index on the clap.
music_rep_padrep_fingers_kick_rim_hats: Left index the kick, left middle the rim, right hand the hats.
music_rep_padrep_fingers_kick_snare: Left index on the kick, right index on the snare.
music_rep_padrep_fingers_sixteenths_ghos: Right index and middle alternate the sixteenths on the hats. Left index the snare and ghosts, left middle the kick.
music_rep_padrep_fingers_split: Right hand on the hats (index and middle alternating). Left index on kick and snare.
music_rep_padrep_five_four_feel: Five beats as 3 + 2: the kick starts each group on 1 and 4 (with a push on the & of 2), the snare closes them on 3 and 5.
music_rep_padrep_fool_in_the_rain_feel: John Bonham's half-time shuffle on a sixteenth-triplet grid (six steps a beat). Shuffled hats, ghosts in the gaps, the backbeat on 3. Provisional: a teaching version, check it against the recording.
music_rep_padrep_four_on_floor_feel: A kick on every beat, the clap on 2 and 4.
music_rep_padrep_funk_150_feel: The tamborzão sped up to 150 BPM (2016 on), with DJ Sany Pitbull's extra kick on the & of 3.
music_rep_padrep_funk_150_fingers: As the tamborzão, lighter on the fingers.
music_rep_padrep_funk_sixteenths_feel: Sixteenth hats over a kick on 1, the a of 1 and the & of 3. Ghosts on the a of 2 and the a of 4.
music_rep_padrep_funky_drummer_feel: Sixteenth hats, ghosted snares around the backbeats, open hats on the a of 2 and 4.
music_rep_padrep_funky_drummer_fingers: Right index and middle alternate the hats. Left index the snare and its ghosts, left middle the kick.
music_rep_padrep_ghost_boom_bap_feel: Ghosts on the a of 2, the e of 3 and the a of 4: soft, under 40% of the backbeat.
music_rep_padrep_house_feel: Closed hat on the beat, open hat on every &; the kick never stops.
music_rep_padrep_house_fingers: Left index on the kick, left middle the clap, right index and middle the two hats.
music_rep_padrep_impeach_feel: Two kicks together on the & of 2 and 3, then an open hat.
music_rep_padrep_independence_feel: The hats never change. The kick takes a new pattern every bar.
music_rep_padrep_kompa_feel: The cowbell is the metronome of kompa, the gong (a muffled floor tom) on 4. Provisional: one band player's notation, tempo not documented.
music_rep_padrep_kompa_fingers: Right index the cowbell, right middle the hats. Left index the floor tom.
music_rep_padrep_levee_feel: Slow and heavy. The kick on the a of 2 is the surprise.
music_rep_padrep_level1_summary: Kick, snare and eighth hats, split hands.
music_rep_padrep_level2_summary: Two-bar hip-hop beats with the kick moving.
music_rep_padrep_level2_title: Boom bap and the first breaks
music_rep_padrep_level3_summary: Soft snares between the backbeats, over sixteenth hats.
music_rep_padrep_level4_summary: Steady hats over a moving kick, fills and MPC swing.
music_rep_padrep_level5_summary: House, trap rolls, drum and bass.
music_rep_padrep_level6_summary: The Amen and Apache breaks, bar by bar.
music_rep_padrep_level7_summary: The triplet grid: blues and half-time shuffles, the swing ride, 12/8.
music_rep_padrep_level8_summary: Grooves in 5/4, 7/4 and 7/8, counted in groups of two and three.
music_rep_padrep_linear_3_over_4_feel: Hat, snare, kick, one at a time in threes over a four-beat bar: no two hits together.
music_rep_padrep_linear_3_over_4_fingers: Right index hats, right middle snare, left index kick.
music_rep_padrep_linear_doubles_feel: R R L L: doubles split between hats and snare ghosts, the kick on 1 and the & of 3.
music_rep_padrep_linear_doubles_fingers: Right index and middle the hats, left index and middle the ghosts. The kick with the left ring.
music_rep_padrep_linear_inverted_feel: R L L R L R R L: the doubles move inside the group, the kick takes the left's stroke on the & of 3.
music_rep_padrep_linear_inverted_fingers: Right hand the hats, left the snare, the kick where the left would play the & of 3.
music_rep_padrep_linear_paradiddle_feel: R L R R L R L L: the paradiddle, the backbeat on the left's stroke, the kick on the right's lead.
music_rep_padrep_linear_paradiddle_finge: Right hand the hats, left the snare, the kick for the right's first stroke of each group.
music_rep_padrep_linear_singles_feel: R L R L: the right hand's strokes on the hats and the backbeat, the left's as ghosts, the kick in place of the right on 1 and 3.
music_rep_padrep_linear_singles_fingers: Right index hats and backbeat, left index ghosts, left middle the kick.
music_rep_padrep_one_beat_fill_feel: A bar of groove, four sixteenths on the snare in its last beat, then crash and kick together on the one.
music_rep_padrep_one_beat_fill_fingers: Right hand hats and the fill, left index kick. Land the crash with the right.
music_rep_padrep_one_drop_feel: Nothing on 1: kick and cross-stick drop together on 3 of a half-time bar, an open hat leading into the next. Often played with a shuffle.
music_rep_padrep_paradiddle_split_feel: RLRR LRLL with the right hand on the snare and the left on the hats: a sticking that sounds like a groove.
music_rep_padrep_paradiddle_split_finger: Right index on the snare, left index on the hats.
music_rep_padrep_purdie_feel: Bernard Purdie's half-time shuffle: ghosts on the middle triplet, the backbeat on 3, the kick on 1 and the last triplets of 2 and 4. Tempo approximate.
music_rep_padrep_reggaeton_feel: The dembow: a kick on every beat, the snare's 3+3+2 over it, a deep tom on 1 and 3.
music_rep_padrep_reggaeton_fingers: Left index the kick, right index the snare, left middle the tom, right middle the hat.
music_rep_padrep_rock_open_hat_feel: Basic rock with the hat opened on the & of 4 and closed by the next bar's first hat: the lift into each bar.
music_rep_padrep_rock_open_hat_fingers: Right index the closed hat, right middle the open one. Left index kick and snare.
music_rep_padrep_rosanna_feel: Jeff Porcaro's half-time shuffle, built on Purdie's. Ghosts on the middle triplets, the backbeat on 3, a kick that answers itself over two bars. Provisional: a teaching version, check it against the recording.
music_rep_padrep_rumba_clave_feel: The son clave with its third note a sixteenth later: the rumba's lean.
music_rep_padrep_samba_feel: The surdo on the kick (the first and last sixteenth of each beat), a busy hat line and the pedal hat on every &. Tempo approximate.
music_rep_padrep_samba_fingers: Left index and middle the kick figure, right hand the hats, left ring the pedal hat.
music_rep_padrep_seven_eight_feel: Seven eighths as 2 + 2 + 3, the click on every eighth: kick on 1, snare on 3, kick on 5, snare on 6.
music_rep_padrep_seven_four_feel: Seven beats as 4 + 3. Kick and snare alternate, so one bar ends on a kick and the next starts on one. That stumble makes 7 feel like 7.
music_rep_padrep_shave_tag_feel: Shave and a haircut, two bits: the vaudeville ending (Charles Hale, 1899) every drummer plays to close a tune.
music_rep_padrep_shave_tag_fingers: Right hand across snare and toms, left index the kick under the last crash.
music_rep_padrep_shuffle_ghosts_feel: The blues shuffle with a snare ghost on the third triplet of 1 and 3, leading into each backbeat. Keep the ghosts under 40%.
music_rep_padrep_slow_blues_feel: Twelve eighths a bar, the click on every third: kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, the hats on every eighth.
music_rep_padrep_snare_build_feel: Quarters, then eighths, then two bars of sixteenths over four on the floor, and the crash on the drop.
music_rep_padrep_snare_build_fingers: Alternate right index and middle on the snare. Left index keeps the kick.
music_rep_padrep_soca_feel: Four on the floor with the 3+3+2 snare and an open hat sizzling on every &. (Teachers vary the hats: this is Boston Drum Lessons' version.)
music_rep_padrep_soca_fingers: Right index and middle the hats, opening on the &; left index kick, left middle snare.
music_rep_padrep_son_clave_feel: Three then two: the rhythm Cuban music, salsa and the Bo Diddley beat hang on.
music_rep_padrep_son_clave_fingers: Right index on the rim. Count the sixteenths quietly.
music_rep_padrep_songo_feel: Cuban songo: the bell on the beat, the kick on the & of 2 and on 4 like the bass's tumbao. The snare talks around them, with the low tom on 4 and its &. Provisional: one teaching version of many.
music_rep_padrep_songo_fingers: Right index the bell. Left index the snare, left middle the kick, right middle the tom.
music_rep_padrep_steppers_feel: A kick on every beat under the cross-stick on 3: the marching reggae beat.
music_rep_padrep_stomp_clap_feel: Two stomps and a clap, the oldest crowd rhythm there is.
music_rep_padrep_swing_56_feel: Every second sixteenth a little late: loose, not yet a shuffle.
music_rep_padrep_swing_56_fingers: Right index and middle alternate the hats, the middle a touch late.
music_rep_padrep_swing_62_feel: Nearer the triplet: the hip-hop lilt.
music_rep_padrep_swing_62_fingers: Right index and middle alternate the hats. Feel the late one, don't count it.
music_rep_padrep_swing_ride_feel: Ding, ding-a ding, ding-a: the ride on every beat and the last triplet of 2 and 4. The hat foot on 2 and 4, the kick feathered soft on every beat.
music_rep_padrep_swing_ride_fingers: Right index the ride. Left index the pedal hat, left middle the kick, soft.
music_rep_padrep_tamborzao_feel: "Tum pa-pá pum pá": a tresillo of drum skins (1, the a of 1, the & of 2) answered on 3 and 4, no hats, no snare. DJ Luciano Oliveira's own reduction.
music_rep_padrep_tamborzao_fingers: Left index the kick and rack tom, right index and middle the conga (high tom), left middle the floor tom.
music_rep_padrep_think_feel: The "Yeah! Woo!" break: one kick, the snare on 2 and 4, ghosts on the a of 2 and the & of 3. The sixteenths (a tambourine on the recording) sit a little behind the beat.
music_rep_padrep_tony_allen_feel: Fela's drummer: kicks in pairs, a snare line of its own, the hand on the hats and the foot on the pedal hat all independent. Tempo approximate.
music_rep_padrep_tony_allen_fingers: Right index and middle the hats, left index the snare, left middle the kick, left ring the pedal hat. Learn it in Wait mode first.
music_rep_padrep_trap_32_feel: Half time: the clap on 3. The last beat of hats rolls in thirty-seconds.
music_rep_padrep_trap_32_fingers: The roll: right index and middle as a two-finger roll on one pad (or hold Note Repeat at 1/32).
music_rep_padrep_trap_triplet_feel: The same beat, the roll in sixteenth triplets (1/16T).
music_rep_padrep_trap_triplet_fingers: Two-finger roll, six to the beat.
music_rep_padrep_tresillo_backbeat_feel: Three-three-two in the kick against the snare on 2 and 4: the root of reggaeton, New Orleans and much of pop.
music_rep_padrep_turnaround_fill_feel: Three bars and a fill that turns the phrase around.
music_rep_padrep_zouk_feel: Sixteenth hats, loud and soft. The tibwa's cinquillo on the rim. Snare only on 2 and 4.
music_rep_padrep_zouk_fingers: Right index and middle the hats (index loud, middle soft). Left index kick, left middle snare, left ring rim.
music_rep_padskills_dyn_crescendo: Crescendo: a bar of sixteenths, soft to loud
music_rep_padskills_dyn_even: Even: sixteen hits at the same level
music_rep_padskills_dyn_ladder: Four levels: four hits each, soft to loud
music_rep_padskills_fill_down_toms: Sixteenths down the toms on 3 and 4
music_rep_padskills_fill_whole_bar: A bar of sixteenths around the kit
music_rep_padskills_line_clave: Son clave held, the kick moves
music_rep_padskills_orch_hats_snare_deta: Right on the hats, left on the snare, kick under the accents
music_rep_padskills_orch_ride_snare_deta: Right on the ride, left on the snare, kick under the accents
music_rep_padskills_orch_toms_lead_detai: Each group's first stroke on a tom, the rest hats and snare
music_rep_phrases_source_bach_suite_no_2: Bach, Suite No. 2 BWV 1067 (about 1738), a fifth down in E minor
music_rep_phrases_source_bizet_1872_the_: Bizet (1872), the alto part as printed
music_rep_phrases_source_gluck_1774_a_fi: Gluck (1774), a fifth down in Bb
music_rep_phrases_source_grieg_1888_flut: Grieg (1888), Flute I, an octave down
music_rep_phrases_source_joplin_1902_the: Joplin (1902), the octave run folded down
music_rep_phrases_source_mussorgsky_1874: Mussorgsky (1874), scored for alto sax by Ravel (1922); written for alto
music_rep_phrases_title_blues_scale_down: Blues scale down, blue third up
music_rep_phrases_title_blues_scale_run_: Blues scale run with the flat five
music_rep_phrases_title_c_to_d_and_back: C to D and back to A
music_rep_phrases_title_d_minor_lick_1_a: D minor lick 1: a long tone and a fall
music_rep_phrases_title_d_minor_lick_2_t: D minor lick 2: the Dorian sixth
music_rep_phrases_title_d_minor_lick_4_d: D minor lick 4: Dorian run to the top
music_rep_phrases_title_d_minor_lick_5_q: D minor lick 5: question and answer
music_rep_phrases_title_d_minor_lick_6_o: D minor lick 6: over the Dm to G vamp
music_rep_phrases_user_why: Saved from {from}. Take it through the keys.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_arlesien: The flute and harp solo every flutist knows.
The first famous orchestral saxophone solo, high and singing.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_au_clair: Five notes, long values: a breath-control tune.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_badineri: The flute showpiece and audition piece: crisp sixteenths in two.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_bebop_en: The core bebop device: circle the target from above and below, then land.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_blessed_: The gentle minuet flutists learn early: long lines on one breath.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_bolero: The most famous crescendo there is. The tenor and soprano saxophones take the theme.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_bumblebe: The chromatic run everyone recognises, at practice speed.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_c_blues_: The blues scale from the top, then the minor third bending into the major.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_e_minor_: Up the pentatonic and back: the shape behind most rock and pop sax lines.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_entertai: The ragtime hook, from Joplin's own 1902 edition.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_g_blues_: First improvising vocabulary on the horn: the blue note and back.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_honk_rif: Low tonic honks, the flat seventh under them, and the blue third: the bar-walking sax sound.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_hot_cros: The first saxophone tune: B, A and G with the left hand alone.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_ii_v_i: Up Dm7, down G7, and the F and D# closing in on E: a whole bebop sentence.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_lightly_: An early band-book tune: down the left hand and back up.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_maple_le: The rag that made ragtime: the opening's jumping figure.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_morning_: The best-known flute melody in the orchestra: the sunrise in Peer Gynt.
music_rep_phrases_why_aerophone_old_cast: The alto saxophone's lament in Pictures at an Exhibition.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_a_blues_lic: Up to the root and back down the box: the first lick to own.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_add9_moves: G, Cadd9, Dsus4 and Em7 with the ring and pinky fingers anchored on strings 2 and 1 at fret 3: the acoustic pop change.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_amazing_gra: The first melody in three, on the open strings.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_blues_scale: Box 1 up and down from the low A with the E flat between D and E: the blue note in passing.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_blues_turna: The descending double stops over a held A that end every twelve-bar.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_boogie_shuf: The fifth rocking to the sixth on the low strings: the first rhythm riff.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_boom_chuck: Bass note, strum, bass note, strum: the first picking-and-strumming pattern.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_d_dorian_ru: D Dorian from D to D an octave up, eighths, then hang on the top note.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_d_dorian_si: Climb to B natural, the note that turns D minor into Dorian, then step back down to D.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_d_dorian_va: B and D outline the G chord of the vamp, then E falls to D: Dorian heard as chord tones.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_d_minor_ans: Up to D and back, then the same rhythm answered lower, ending on the root.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_d_minor_lon: Hold the high D, fall through the box, sustain the A: let the note sing before moving.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_d_minor_oct: D, C and A each with its octave two strings up: a thick, singing line from two notes.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_double_stop: Two strings at the fifth fret, hammered in eighths, then walking down: the shared rock and roll intro.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_g_run: The most played run in bluegrass, the tag at the end of a line.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_hammer_on_c: Strum the chord with one finger still lifted, then hammer it down: the decoration soul and rock players hang on Am, C, Em and D.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_minor_third: The minor third rubbing against the root on the G and D strings, twice, then home.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_ode_to_joy: The first melody in most open-position methods.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_pentatonic_: Pattern 1 at the fifth fret, the box every lead player starts from.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_root_b7_5: A, G, E from the top of box 1, twice, then down to the low A: the shape of a hundred blues licks.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_spanish_rom: The classic first classical piece. This is its melody on the top string.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_sus_to_majo: Dsus4, D, Dsus2, D, then the same on A: one finger lifting and landing on the top strings while the chord rings.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_texas_shuff: The low-string boogie stretched to 5, 6, flat 7, 6 in a hard long-short shuffle, through E, A, E and B: the engine under Texas blues. A click to each dotted quarter.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_travis_c_am: The gateway fingerpicking pattern: thumb on the bass, fingers between.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_twinkle: A first melody on the top two strings.
music_rep_phrases_why_guitar_walking_boo: The single-note rhythm riff under a twelve-bar, on A then D.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_alberti: The left-hand figure under half of Mozart and Haydn.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_amen_ending: The plagal close over a held tonic, with the minor four on the way home: the Amen at the end of a hymn or a gospel tune.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_blues_ending: The top line slides down from the root to the fifth over the bass, then the flat II seventh falls into the tonic: the way a blues says goodbye.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_blues_shuffl: Fifths and sixths rocking under a twelve-bar: the left hand of every blues piano player, on C then F.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_blues_turnar: I, I7, IV, sharp IV diminished, I, VI7, ii, V7: the last four bars of a blues, the left hand walking up under them.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_boogie_bass: The first left-hand groove in blues and jazz methods: up the chord and back, then the same on IV.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_c_blues_lick: First improvising vocabulary: up the blues scale and home.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_canon_chords: Pachelbel's eight chords, the most borrowed progression there is, a chord a beat.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_fill_grace_s: A quick slide from the flat third into the third, then the fifth and home: the crushed note of blues and pop piano.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_fill_octave_: Octaves climbing 5, 6, 7 into the tonic on the next downbeat: the pickup that lifts a ballad into its next phrase.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_fill_pentato: A major pentatonic run in sixteenths from the top, filling the bar before the next phrase lands on the chord.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_fur_elise: The most requested hook once the basics are in.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_gospel_653: Six, five, three, then again an octave down, landing on the chord: the most used gospel run.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_gospel_octav: The right hand rocks between thumb and pinky an octave apart to sustain the top note, then lands on the chord.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_gospel_penta: Down the major pentatonic with a grace note into each third: the run a gospel player throws in between lines.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_greensleeves: The standard minor-key piece in three.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_happy_birthd: You'll be asked to play it.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_i_vi_iv_v: The four chords under a thousand songs, voiced close so the hand barely moves.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_jingle_bells: The seasonal hook everyone asks for.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_mountain_kin: The creeping build-up loop: the same line, faster each time.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_nachtmusik: Instantly recognised: a rising G major arpeggio, answered.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_ode_to_joy: A first-month staple in every method: steps only, one dotted rhythm.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_rock_octave_: Right-hand octaves down the major scale in eighths, landing on the chord: the big fill of a rock ballad.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_rock_triplet: The right hand pounds a chord in triplets while the left hand walks a boogie: 1950s rock and roll piano. Written in 12/8, a click to each group of three.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_rock_turn_wa: A turn around the fifth that falls to the root in 3/4, the right-hand fill of a piano-bar waltz, then the chord.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_seven_three_: Six roots a fifth apart walking home, the right hand moving a note or two each time: the turnaround under gospel and soul endings.
music_rep_phrases_why_piano_twinkle: The universal first tune: five fingers, one hand position.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_amazing_gr: A slow melody in three, all in first position.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_blues_doub: Two strings at once, G and C to E and A, then a walk up to A.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_blues_pent: Down the A minor pentatonic from D to C, landing on A: the first ukulele blues lick.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_blues_turn: A high A over a line falling on the C string, then A to E7: the end of every twelve-bar.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_campanella: The open G and A strings ring under the scale: the harp sound of high-G fingerstyle.
Five notes a string apart, so every one rings: the scale behind Cripple Creek.
The minor campanella scale of the higher grades: B flat and D on the G string, C sharp on the A.
Neighbouring notes on neighbouring strings: F rings under E, G under A.
The first tune again, with G and A on the open outer strings so they ring.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_chord_melo: The melody note on top of each chord shape, single notes between: the first chord-melody arrangement.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_four_chord: The four first ukulele chords, two beats each.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_happy_birt: You'll be asked to play it, on the re-entrant G string.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_hawaiian_v: D7, G7, C: the stock intro and ending of a Hawaiian tune.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_island_str: Down, down-up, up-down-up: the signature ukulele strum, on one chord.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_mary: The method-book staple: three notes, then two more.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_ode_to_joy: All in first position on the C and E strings.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_oh_susanna: The campfire tune: quick pickups and a dotted rhythm.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_picking_c_: The first picking pattern: thumb on the G string, fingers across.
music_rep_phrases_why_ukulele_saints: The first song in many ukulele books.
music_rep_rhythm_groove_trap: Trap: the snare on 3, the 808 around it
music_rep_score_improv_game_approach_abo: A chord tone on every beat 1, approached by a half step from below or above. The score is the share of bars.
music_rep_score_improv_game_blues_scale_: Only the key's blues scale (1, b3, 4, b5, 5, b7). The score is the share of notes in it.
music_rep_score_improv_game_bridge_about: Rest or play the head in the A sections and improvise only the bridge, a 3rd or 7th within a beat of 85% of its changes. Pick a tune with a bridge (rhythm changes, Satin Doll).
music_rep_score_improv_game_call_respons: The band plays a two-bar call, you answer in the next two. Every answer starts in its bars and ends before the next call.
music_rep_score_improv_game_changes_abou: Chord tones on 75% of beats 1 and 3, and a 3rd or 7th within a beat of 70% of the changes.
music_rep_score_improv_game_chord_tones_: Lines through the changes with a chord tone on every beat 1 and 3. The score is the share that are.
music_rep_score_improv_game_displacement: One short motif of two to six notes, each time a beat later in the bar (the Straight, No Chaser idea). The aim is a displaced motif in two bars of every three.
music_rep_score_improv_game_free_about: Solo freely. Scored on chord tones on beats 1 and 3, a 3rd or 7th on each change, time on the grid and a rest every four bars.
music_rep_score_improv_game_guide_tones_: Play only 3rds and 7ths, one or two a bar, and land one within a beat of 80% of the changes.
music_rep_score_improv_game_melody_fills: Play the head, and fill only its rests of two beats or more with two to four notes: 90% of the melody's notes, and a fill in six rests (every rest, when it has fewer). Needs one of your scores with its melody.
music_rep_score_improv_game_motif_about: Keep one bar's rhythm (the C Jam riff, or the Charleston) and change the pitches to fit each chord: the same rhythm in 8 of 12 bars, a chord tone on beat 1 in 75%.
music_rep_score_improv_game_off_beat_abo: Start every phrase off the beat, on the and-of-1 or the and-of-4. The score is the share that do.
music_rep_score_improv_game_pentatonic_1: Only the minor pentatonic on the key's tonic (D minor pentatonic over D dorian).
music_rep_score_improv_game_pentatonic_2: Only the minor pentatonic a step above the tonic (E minor pentatonic over D dorian).
music_rep_score_improv_game_pentatonic_5: Only the minor pentatonic a fifth above the tonic (A minor pentatonic over D dorian).
music_rep_score_improv_game_quote_about: Open each A section with a fragment of the tune's melody (four notes or more, its pitches in any octave), then develop it. Needs one of your scores with its melody.
music_rep_score_improv_game_side_slip_ab: Slip a phrase a half step up (three or more notes outside the scale) for about two beats, then resolve to a chord tone on the next beat. Four slips a chorus, every one resolved.
music_rep_score_improv_game_space_1_abou: Play one bar, rest one, the whole chorus. The score is the share of bars kept.
music_rep_score_improv_game_space_about: Play two bars, rest two, the whole chorus. The score is the share of bars kept.
music_rep_score_improv_game_thirds_about: Land on the 3rd of each new chord, within a beat of the change. The score is the share of changes landed.
music_rep_score_improv_game_three_notes_: Only the key's 1, b3 and 5 (F, Ab, C in F), 90% of your notes, with at least six two-beat rests a chorus.
music_rep_score_improv_headline_silent: Nothing was played, so nothing passed.

music_rep_score_improv_metric_displaced: The motif, a beat later each time
music_rep_score_improv_metric_downbeats: A chord tone on each bar's beat 1
music_rep_score_improv_metric_fills: Rests in the head filled with 2 to 4 notes
music_rep_score_improv_metric_quotes: A sections opened with a fragment of the head
music_rep_score_improv_metric_resolved: Slips resolved to a chord tone on the beat
music_rep_score_improv_metric_windows: Bars kept (playing in yours, silent in the band's)
music_rep_score_improv_no_head_rests: the head has no two-beat rests
music_rep_score_jam_on_chord: {counts} Most notes landed on the chord.
music_rep_score_jam_outside: {counts} Many notes sat outside the scale; aim for a chord tone on each change.
music_rep_score_jam_try_landing: {counts} Try landing on a chord tone as each chord arrives.

music_rep_score_too_few: too few notes landed to judge
music_rep_strums_backbeat_chuck: accents on 2 and 4, a fretting-hand chuck
music_rep_strums_bossa: bossa, thumb on 1 and 3, fingers off the beat
music_rep_strums_calypso: calypso, D DU UDU with the push on 3 and
music_rep_strums_fan: fan stroke, a four-finger roll on 1 and 3
music_rep_strums_reggae: reggae, short strums on the and
music_rep_strums_split_stroke: Formby split stroke, D dU D dU, accent on the up
music_rep_strums_swing: swing, D then DU DU DU swung
music_rep_strums_swing_comp: swing comping, four to the bar, chuck on 2 and 4
music_rep_strums_triple_stroke: triple stroke study, triplets on 1 and 3
music_rep_strums_triplet: triplet strum, i down, thumb down, i up
music_rep_studio_chop_amen_detail: All four bars: a beat a slice
music_rep_studio_chop_boom_bap_detail: One bar of the kit: a sixteenth a slice
music_rep_studio_chop_funky_drummer_deta: One bar, ghosts and open hats: a sixteenth a slice
music_rep_studio_chop_keys_detail: Two bars of a minor seventh riff: an eighth a slice
music_rep_studio_edit_flip: Flip: the first beat twice, then the back half
music_rep_studio_edit_stutter: Stutter: some beats repeat their opening slices
music_rep_studio_end_stop: A stop: crash and kick on the one
music_rep_studio_exercise_free_detail: Four bars of your own, then play them again
music_rep_studio_exercise_order_detail: Replay the slices 1 to 16 to the click: the loop comes back
music_rep_studio_exercise_reorder_detail: Play the slices in the order written
music_rep_studio_feel_shuffle_hint: Long-short on every beat: the first and last of each triplet.
music_rep_studio_feel_swung_hint: The ride's long-short swing: ding, ding-a ding.
music_rep_studio_feel_twelve_eight_hint: Every triplet played, slow: twelve eighths a bar.
music_rep_studio_form_break_set: Breaks: intro, boom bap, Funky Drummer, out
music_rep_studio_repeat_build_detail: Hold the snare: two bars at 1/8, two at 1/16, louder all the way, then the crash and kick on the drop
music_rep_studio_repeat_rolls_detail: Hats in eighths. Hold the pad for each roll, at the written rate
music_rep_winds_lesson_octave: The octave key: G to D
music_rep_winds_lesson_palm: The palm keys: C#6 to F6
